a:r.a:t: Vitamin D Is Synthesized from Cholesterol and Regulates Calcium Metabolism

p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram showing the steps in Vitamin D synthesis with structures included. (a) The process begins with 7-dehydrocholesterol, labeled below. The carbons are numbered beginning with the top carbon on the A ring at the far left. The A ring solid wedge bonds at carbon 3 on the lower right to OH, which is shaded blue. This is the polar head group. The A ring bonds right to the B ring, which has a double bond between carbons 5 and 6. Between the tops of the two rings is a solid wedge bond that makes C19. At C9, there is a dashed wedge bond down to H, so that it reaches down into the B ring. The bond between C8 and C9 bonds up and right to the C ring. C ring has a solid wedge bonded H on C8, the bottom point of the ring. Bonds between C13 and C14, to the right, bond to ring D, which has 5 sides. Between the tops of ring C and D is an upward solid wedge bond that makes C18. This ring region is the steroid nucleus, labeled below. At the apex of ring D (on C17), C17 dashed wedge bonds up and right to H, and up to C20. This begins the alkyl side chain, labeled right. C20 dashed wedge bonds up and left to C21, solid wedge bonds up to H, and bonds up and right to the side chain, which has C23-C27. The bond between carbons 9 and 10 on the B ring is shaded orange. Two right arrows are labeled "2 steps (in skin)" with a wavy arrow above indicating the input of UV light. To the right, (b) the next structure is cholcalciferol (Vitamin D3) (labeled below). Here, the B ring of 7-dehydrocholesterol has been broken, so it appears now as 2 cis double bonds between the A and C rings (C6 and C7). C10, on the A ring, now double bonds up and right to C18. Two right arrows are labeled "1 step in the liver, 1 step in the kidney" to show the next steps in the process. To the right, (c) 1-alpha, 25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 (calcitrol) (labeled below). This structure is the same as described in (b), but it now has an OH bonded right to C25 (part of the alkyl chain) and down and right as a dashed wedge bond to C1 on the A ring.
